notes:
Summary: Mid-market product analytics SaaS. Evaluated Hosted API first (fast onboarding), moved to Dedicated for predictable unit economics and EU data residency.

POC highlights: quick results on embeddings + reranking. Latency targets: 95th <120ms for typical chat flows, p95 for reranking <200ms under 1500 TPS equivalent traffic. Throughput target: sustain 2k tokens/sec for peak routes. Cost sensitivity: need predictable monthly committed spend; target blended cost <$0.0008/token for primary chat model.

Dedicated pricing ask (negotiation points):
- Proposed base commitment: equivalent of 4 reserved GPU seats (8x A10-equivalent or 2x A100-40 equiv) delivered as "Committed Units".
- Ramp schedule: 3-month ramp from 50% -> 100% usage with pro-rated commit credits month 1 and 2. OakBridge requests 25% credit on unused commit in month 1 and 10% month 2 while traffic ramps.
- Burst: allowed burst up to 2.5x baseline for up to 72 hours/month. Billing for burst above commit at overage rate = 1.5x list (negotiable). OakBridge asks for a 30% discount on the first 10 burst hours during initial 6 months.
- Overage terms: over-commit usage billed daily, invoiced monthly; preference for predictable bucket pricing vs per-token unpredictability.
- Contract term: 12 months preferred; open to 24 months for deeper discounts.

Security/compliance: require SSO/SAML integration, SOC2 attestation, audit logs forwarded to their SIEM, KMS integration for model keys, and EU data residency for PII.

Commercial tone quotes: CTO - "We need predictable unit economics; can't be pinged with per-token bills every month." Head of ML - "If we can get stable latency at price X, we can fold this into product pricing."

Open action items:
- Redwood to provide a redline-friendly SOW + explicit ramp credit language (due 2026-03-15).
- Finance to model ARR scenarios for 12 vs 24 month commit (OakBridge finance looped).
- SE to run one extended high-concurrency run (48h) on Dedicated staging once infra provisioned to validate burst behavior.
- Legal: resolve IP/data residency addendum (OakBridge redlines received).

Stated blockers: legal IP clause (they want indemnity around user-generated content), procurement window (Q2 budget), and clarification on how burst is metered (per-GPU-hour vs per-token).

CRM-style fragments: "likes the transparent perf dashboard", "asks for per-route SLOs", "wants optional A/B canary during first 2 weeks", "prefers invoice monthly, net-45".

Suggested Redwood play: propose two SKU offers - (A) 12m base commit with 3-month ramp + initial burst credit, (B) 24m deeper discount + rolling over 10% unused commit credit. Include clear overage math in examples (monthly traffic scenarios).
